A chart tells a story when the annotations do the pointing: a threshold line, a named outlier, a shaded period, a title that states the finding.
These examples cover reference lines, text and boxed labels, ad-hoc [`annotate`](../reference/geoms/annotate.qmd) layers, cluster marks, and free-form shapes drawn from coordinates.
Write titles as findings rather than descriptions, and annotate the few points that matter instead of labelling everything.
Every example ships its full source: click **View source** to copy it.
